Pilot, crews while summoning sick, and is offered by the packet; and the
load-time guards. Test cards live in `tests/data/crew_power_bonus.cards.json`.

## Station, the cost — "put charge counters equal to its power"

### Overview

Uthros, Titanic Godcore and Adagia, Windswept Bastion, the two Planets in the
Bard, King of Dale deck: *"Station (Tap another creature you control: Put charge
counters equal to its power on this Planet. Station only as a sorcery.)"* Rule
702.184a. The first of two capabilities Station needs; the "12+ |" threshold is
the second.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `tap_permanents` already charged "tap another creature you control", but it
  was write-only: the creature was tapped and forgotten, so no effect could ask
  its power.
- `choose_permanents` + the `tap` op pays on resolution, so the ability could be
  activated with nothing to tap and responded to before anything tapped.
- A snapshot at payment misses a pump in response; a bare oid reads the
  graveyard card's printed power once the creature has gone. The release notes
  require both the live read and last-known information.

### The shape

`tap_permanents.as` names the one tapped permanent. `costs.pay` takes a
`bindings` dict, `game._activate` hands it to `push_activated_ability`, and the
binding is `{"paid_object": key}` pointing at a record in
`GameState.paid_objects`. `zones.move_object` writes the departing permanent's
derived power and toughness into any open record for it; `values._characteristic`
reads the live permanent while the record is open and the record once it is
filled. `_resolve_ability` prunes the records its item carried. `add_counters`
clamps a negative amount to zero (107.1b).

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_station.py`: offered with a creature and not without one, not
with only tapped creatures, only at sorcery speed; the creature tapped before
resolution; counters equal to the tapped creature's power and not another's; a
second activation adding; a pump in response counting; a pumped creature
destroyed in response using its last-known power; negative power putting none
and removing none; the record pruned; and the load-time guards. The test card is
`tests/data/station.cards.json`.

## Station symbols — "12+ | …", an ability had only at a counter count

### Overview

The second half of Station, rule 721: "As long as this permanent has N or more
charge counters on it, it has [abilities]." Uthros, Titanic Godcore's
"12+ | {U}, {T}: Add {U} for each artifact you control." and Adagia, Windswept
Bastion's "12+ | {3}{W}, {T}: Create a token that's a copy of target artifact or
enchantment you control, except it's legendary. Activate only as a sorcery."

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

`condition` ("activate only if…") refuses the activation of an ability the
permanent still has. Uthros's gated line is a mana ability, and mana abilities
never pass through that check, so it would have tapped for blue from turn one.
The rule is about existence, not permission.

### The shape

`threshold: {"counter": "charge", "at_least": 12}` on an activated ability,
compiled to `Ability.threshold`. `characteristics.present_printed_abilities`
drops the gated abilities an object does not meet (all of them off the
battlefield) from `abilities_of` and `_derived_abilities`, which legality, the
mana solver, the by-hand mana path, the AI and granted-ability provenance all
read. `legality._ability_aims` checks it too, for `_offers_something_else`,
which walks the printed face. Resolution is untouched: `ability_of` reads the
printed list, so an ability on the stack survives losing the counters.

The loader refuses a threshold on anything but an activated ability, on a
grantable ability, an ungated ability after a gated one, and falling or
mixed-counter thresholds: abilities are addressed by index, so an absent one may
only drop a tail. `verify._covered` claims an `N+ |` line only through an ability
gated at N whose text is the whole line. The activation sweep in
`tests/cards/test_every_card_works.py` stocks the counters a threshold asks for,
and its target prop now reads `any_types` ("target artifact or enchantment").

### Not built

Spacecraft becoming artifact creatures with a base P/T at their number, and gated
keywords, statics and triggers. Neither Planet needs them; the loader refuses a
gated non-activated ability.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_station_threshold.py`: absent below 4 and present at exactly 4;
the 12+ mana ability absent at 11 and present at 12 at its printed index; Station
still offered past the last number; no striations in hand; removing a counter
taking the ability away; an ability on the stack resolving after its counters
are gone; the 12+ mana ability adding one blue per artifact and absent from the
by-hand mana path at 11; the load-time guards; and the residual gate (the
striated card claims every line, an ungated ability or a gate at another number
does not).

Neither card is authored in this change.

## Granted activated abilities — a chapter that gives the Saga something to activate

### Overview

Urza's Saga: *"I — This Saga gains "{T}: Add {C}." II — This Saga gains "{2},
{T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token
gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.'""* A chapter resolves once and the
gain outlives it, until the Saga leaves the battlefield (400.7). The gap record
said chapter I "loads today"; it loaded and did nothing.

### The two holes

- **The op's grants never reached `abilities_of`.** `primitives.grant_ability`
  writes a pointer onto the permanent, and only `triggers.collect` read it.
  Legality, `costs.mana_sources` and `game._activate` read
  `characteristics.abilities_of`, which appended *static* grants only. The op's
  activated grants are now appended there too, with `(granter oid, pool index)`
  provenance — and only its activated ones, since its triggered grants are
  already yielded by `triggers.collect` and would otherwise fire twice.
- **`stack.ability_of` resolved an activated ability off the printed list.**
  That is why `grantable_abilities` refused any activated ability that was not a
  mana ability (605.3a keeps those off the stack). `push_activated_ability` now
  reads the derived list and records `granted_by` plus the index into the
  granter's `grantable_abilities` — the pair a granted trigger already carried —
  and `StackItem.granted_def_id` for a token granter that has ceased to exist.
  On Urza's Saga the old lookup would have resolved the Construct ability as
  chapter II, and `sagas.chapter_on_stack` would then have held off 704.5s: the
  Saga would not be sacrificed after III while a Construct was on its way.

### Refused at load

A granted activated ability with `active_zones` other than the battlefield
(granted cycling): a grant lives on a permanent, so it would never be offered.
A granted chapter stays refused.

### Tier

A — no new op, decision kind, event or API field, nothing under `frontend/`. The
loader refusal is lifted and two engine readers learn the op's grants.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_granted_activated_abilities.py`, on `t_granting_saga`
(`tests/data/granted_activated.cards.json`), which is Urza's Saga as the card
will be written: played as a land it enters with its lore counter; chapter I's
mana ability reaches the solver and survives cleanup; chapter II's ability is
offered at its derived position, goes on the stack carrying its granter, and
makes a 1/1 Construct — also after the Saga has left, and with the granter
object gone; it is not mistaken for a chapter, so the Saga is sacrificed after
III with the Construct still arriving; and a Saga that leaves and returns has
neither grant until chapter I runs again. The two loader tests that pinned the
old refusal (`test_restricted_mana.py`, `test_lose_all_abilities.py`) now pin
the reversal.

## `or_planeswalker` — a token attacking "that player or a planeswalker they control"

### Overview

Adeline, Resplendent Cathar was blocked on "…create a 1/1 white Human creature
token that's tapped and attacking that player or a planeswalker they control."
`attacking` could name a seat (Ainok Strike Leader) and nothing else, although a
declared attacker has been able to attack a planeswalker since planeswalkers
shipped.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `attacking` resolves through `_attacking_player` to a single **pid**; every
  caller writes that pid into `combat.attackers` and no key on any op aims an
  attacker at a permanent.
- Writing only the seat is a narrower card: 506.2 makes a planeswalker a third
  attack target, and this engine already refuses to treat attacking a walker as
  attacking its controller (Ghostly Prison, goad).

### The shape

- **`or_planeswalker: true`** beside `attacking` on `create_token`,
  `copy_permanent` and `put_onto_battlefield`, read by
  `board_helpers._aim_at_planeswalker` after the permanents arrive.
- **The choice is 508.4's**: the arriving creature's controller picks the seat or
  one of that seat's planeswalkers, one question per creature, and no question
  when the seat has no planeswalker.
- **Recorded as a declared attack at a walker is**: `attackers[oid]` stays the
  defending player, `attacking_planeswalker[oid]` names the walker, so damage
  assignment (508.1, 506.4c) and every reader of either map need nothing new —
  including the `attacking_planeswalker` selector being added alongside.

### Tier A, and why no new decision kind

`ask_targets` already poses a mixed list of player and object refs as a
`CHOOSE_OBJECTS`; it gained an optional `purpose` (default `"target"`) so this
question says `"attack"`, since nothing is targeted. The heuristic agent, the RL
encoder, the client's prompt dialog and the authoring verifier all answer a
`CHOOSE_OBJECTS` already, so the verifier cannot hang on it. No event, no API
field, nothing under `frontend/`. The packet's `op_options` are derived from each
op's source, following the helper call, so `or_planeswalker` reaches workers on
all three ops without a hand-written entry.

### The loader guard

`or_planeswalker` without an `attacking` (or with `attacking: false`) is a load
error — the token would attack nobody while the card reads as printed — and so is
a non-boolean value.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_token_attacking_planeswalker.py`: no planeswalker, another
seat's planeswalker, or only your own means no question and the token attacks the
player; with one, the token's controller (not the effect's) is offered exactly the
seat and its walker; choosing the walker records it, choosing the player records
none; two tokens choose separately; `attacking: true` widens the same way; no
attack event fires; `put_onto_battlefield` and `copy_permanent` take the key; the
printed card through real combat puts the Human's damage on the walker, deals
nothing when the walker has left, asks only at the pod seats that have walkers,
and falls back to the player under the passive answer; its `set_pt` power counts
the creatures its controller has; and the load-time guards and packet options.

Adeline is not authored in this change; its gap record stays until she is.

## `mana_cost` — the printed cost, not the number read off it

### Overview

Urza's Saga, chapter III: *"Search your library for an artifact card with mana
cost {0} or {1}, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle."* The closest the
selector language could say was `mana_value <= 1` with `not_colors` over all five
colours and `x_in_mana_cost: false`, and that is a different card: 202.1b gives a
card with no mana symbols **no** mana cost, and 23 artifacts in the catalog are
that shape — Seat of the Synod, Darksteel Citadel and every Bridge among them.
They have mana value 0, so the approximation fetches them; the Saga cannot.

### What it compares

`{"mana_cost": ["{0}", "{1}"]}` — any of a list of printed costs.
`mana.printed_cost_is` compares symbol counts: generic, each coloured slot
(`{C}` included), `{X}`, and each hybrid or Phyrexian pip as itself. So `{1}`
matches one generic symbol and nothing else, a card with no cost matches
nothing, and each wanted cost goes through the parser first, so `" {1} "` and
`"{1}"` agree.

### Where it is read

Everywhere the key is legal, because an unread key loads and matches everything:
`selectors.matches` (effects and targets), `triggers.matches_card_filter`,
`characteristics._matches_printed` (static `affects`, counts, spell filters) and
`cost_reduction._reduction_matches`. An embalm-style copy with "no mana cost" is
honoured on the effect and trigger sides.

### Refused at load

A bare string (iterated it is characters), an empty list, an empty entry ("no
cost" is exactly what never matches) and an unparsable cost — in
`validate_selector` and in every static, spell and counting filter.

### Tier

A — a selector key and its readers. No op, event, decision kind or API field;
nothing under `frontend/`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_mana_cost_selector.py`: {1} and {0} match; an artifact land, an
{X}, a {2}, a {C}, a {W/P} and a {2/W} do not; a pip matches itself; spelling is
normalised; an end-to-end search offers only the {1} from a library holding the
land, the {X} and the {2}; the trigger and static readers agree; and the load
refusals. `t_granting_saga`'s chapter III now uses the key.

## `strive` — a cost that grows with the targets

### Overview

Call the Coppercoats: *"Strive — This spell costs {1}{W} more to cast for each
target beyond the first. Choose any number of target opponents. …"* The same
first line is on the Journey into Nyx strive cycle (Launch the Fleet, Twinflame,
Ajani's Presence and the rest), each with one "any number of target" spec.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `cost_reduction` only subtracts, and every head it has reads the battlefield,
  never the spell's own targets.
- `multikicker` repeats a price, but the caster picks the count independently of
  the targets, so a three-target cast that paid nothing extra would load clean.
- Nothing in legality could price a line by its targets: `_cast_variant` solved
  one payment and attached it to every target tuple.

### The shape

- **`strive: "{1}{W}"`** on `CardModel` and `CardDef`, kept out of `mana_cost`
  so mana value stays printed.
- **`casting.strive_surcharge(card, targets)`**: the surcharge scaled by
  `len(targets) - 1`, or nothing for zero or one target. `Game._cast` adds it to
  whichever cost the chosen branch picked (601.2f: an increase applies to every
  way of casting).
- **`casting._priced_tuples`** replaces the single solve in `_cast_variant`. For
  a card without strive it is the old behaviour exactly: one payment, every
  tuple. For strive it solves zero, one, two… extra targets and stops at the
  first it cannot pay, then re-enumerates the tuples **one size at a time**
  (`enumerate_target_tuples(..., size_cap=n)`, keeping only size `n`), largest
  first, empty tuple last. A count the caster cannot pay is never offered, and
  each line's `pays` names the lands its own count would tap.
- **`size_cap`** on `enumerate_target_tuples` bounds a variable-size spec. It had
  to bound the enumeration rather than filter the result: subsets come largest
  first and are cut at `MAX_TARGET_OPTIONS`, so with six creatures every kept
  tuple is a four-or-more pick, and single targets — the line that costs nothing
  extra — are pushed out even by the fifteen pairs.
- The free resolution-time casts (`suspend.cast_for_free`, and
  `replacements._offer_cast` for madness and miracle) pass `size_cap=1` for a
  strive card: they cannot collect the surcharge, so they take at most one
  target rather than every target with the increase unpaid.

### The loader guard

Exactly one target spec, `count: "any"`, and no mode targets; a free or X strive
is refused; so is strive beside overload, morph, bestow or mutate, each of which
casts with targets the rule supplies.

### Authoring

`strive` joins `CARD_LEVEL_COST_KEYS` in the packet.
`fidelity.unimplemented_mechanics` declares "strive" when the field is set, since
`_MECHANIC_LINE` reads "Strive —" as a mechanic. `verify._covered` claims the
line on a permanent only when the symbols before "more to cast for each target
beyond the first" parse to the declared cost.

### Tier

A card-level cost: no op, event, decision kind or API field, nothing under
`frontend/`. The action already carried its targets, which is all `Game._cast`
needs to charge the right amount.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_strive.py`: one target and zero targets tap three lands, two tap
five, three tap seven; every chosen target is bound; seven lands offer counts
0–3, six offer 0–2, three offer 0–1, two offer nothing; one Plains and four
Islands offer no second target (the surcharge has a colour); the first line is
the largest affordable one; each line's `pays` matches its count; on a six-bear
board five lands still offer one and two targets and charge five for two; a free
cast takes one target; the loader refusals; and the fidelity audit.

Call the Coppercoats is not authored in this change.

### Found along the way, not fixed

Multikicker and replicate's **mana** half is priced by legality
(`cost.plus(branch.mana.scaled(additional_times))` in `_cast_variant`) but never
charged by `Game._cast`, which pays only `additional.without_mana()` per time.
Casting the multikicker test anthem kicked three times on eight Plains taps two
lands. `test_multikicker.py` asserts the offered counts and the read-back count,
not the lands tapped, so nothing fails.

## "Those opponents" — the targeted players as a selector's controller

### Overview

Call the Coppercoats' second sentence: *"Choose any number of target opponents.
Create X 1/1 white Human Soldier creature tokens, where X is the number of
creatures **those opponents** control."* Its gap record asked for a new
"targeted-player selector", reasoning that `controller` accepts only fixed roles.

### What was already there

Nothing new was needed in the engine. A selector's `controller` is a full player
spec (`selectors.matches` hands a Mapping clause to `select_players`), and
`{"target": "t1"}` resolves through `ctx.target_players`, which returns every
player ref under the id rather than the first. Cloak and Dagger's "creature
**they** control" is the same clause with one seat in it. On resolution the
context is built from `targeting.filter_legal`, so 608.2b already applies: a
target that became illegal is not in the set, and a spell whose targets are all
illegal does not resolve.

The gap was written in good faith: the packet named `selector_keys` but never
said what `controller` could hold, and the DSL reference's selector block listed
`you|opponent|any` only.

### What changed

- **`loader.effects._validate_nested_player_refs`**: `_validate_effect` now walks
  an effect's `objects`, `per`, `selector`, `affects`, `amount`, `count`, `power`
  and `toughness` and validates every Mapping `controller`/`player` clause with
  `_validate_player_spec`, wherever it is nested. Before, only the top-level
  `player`/`chooser`/`controller` keys were checked, so
  `{"count": {"controller": {"target": "t9"}}}` loaded and counted nobody, and so
  did a `{"target": …}` naming a `permanent` target.
- **Packet note** spelling the clause for "those opponents" / "they control",
  and naming `controller: "opponent"` as the near miss.
- **Docs**: the selector block's `controller` comment, and a card-dsl section.

### Tier

Loader validation and vocabulary. No op, event, decision or API field; nothing
under `frontend/`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_targeted_players.py`, at a four-seat table with two, three and
four creatures: one target counts that seat; two count both; the untargeted seat
is never counted; all three count everyone; zero targets counts nobody; the
`controller: "opponent"` counterfactual counts the whole table off one target;
protection granted in response drops that seat while the other still counts;
protection on the only target leaves no tokens; and the loader refuses an
undeclared id, a non-player target, and an undeclared id nested inside `not`.

Call the Coppercoats is not authored in this change.

## Classes — levels, level lines and level-gated abilities — 716

### Overview

Caretaker's Talent, and every Class after it: "(Gain the next level as a sorcery
to add its ability.) … / {W}: Level 2 / … / {3}{W}: Level 3 / Creature tokens you
control get +2/+2." Thirty-four Classes in the catalog print the same three-band
shape. This is the first commit of the Class subsystem, built under
`/import-moxfield`'s rule 2 as a sequence of one-capability commits; the
"becomes level N" trigger is the next.

`docs/rules-coverage.md` held no decision about Classes. Its **Level up** row
chose a counter plus a conditional static, and the gap record checked that
spelling in full and refused it: the counter can be bought twice or out of
order, a condition cannot switch a static off, and a `counter_placed` trigger
fires again at level 3.

### The shape

- **`GameObject.class_level`**, 1 by default, set to 1 in
  `zones._enter_battlefield` (716.3), on `to_dict`, and on the card view as
  `level` for a card with level lines (`CardDef.top_level`).
- **`kind: "level"`** in the card format, with `level` and `cost` and nothing
  else (`_LEVEL_LINE_KEYS`). The loader compiles an activated ability with
  `sorcery_speed_only`, the `become_level` effect and `Ability.becomes_level`.
- **`legality._ability_aims`** refuses a level line unless the source is at
  level N-1.
- **`become_level`** sets the level and bumps the characteristics version; a
  source off the battlefield is left alone. Refused in any authored effect.
- **`level: N`** on any other ability becomes `Ability.level`.
  `Ability.present_at` is the gate, applied by `present_printed_abilities` (the
  derived list, with `AbilityKind.LATENT` stand-ins holding seats), by
  `_ability_statics` and by `_active_player_statics`.
- Load-time refusals: no `Class` subtype, a gapped or repeated ladder, a level no
  line reaches, `level: 1`, a gate on a chapter/reflexive ability or off the
  battlefield, and a level on a granted ability.

### Frontend

`CardView.level` in `api/types.ts`, and `counterBadges` leads with "Level N",
so both the board face and the reader panel show it where counters already sit.
Vitest in `tests/cardStyle.test.ts`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_class_levels.py`: the ladder (offered at N-1 only, resolves on
the stack, sorcery speed, paid for, a departed source, set not increment); every
reader of a gated ability (anthem, activated, triggered, player-wide static,
lose-all-abilities); seats kept and `latent` stand-ins; the level is not a
counter, not copied, reset on re-entry and kept on the way out; serialization;
the loader refusals; and `tests/cards/test_every_card_works.py`'s activation
sweep, which learned `_reach_the_level` and is run against the test Class.
`tests/cards/golden_vocabulary.json` gains `become_level` and `_LEVEL_LINE_KEYS`.

## `becomes_level` — "When this Class becomes level N" — 716.4

### Overview

The second commit of the Class subsystem. Eleven of the catalog's thirty-four
Classes print "When this Class becomes level N, …" — Caretaker's Talent's copy of
a token, Wizard Class's two cards, Cleric Class's reanimation — and it is usually
the payoff for buying the level.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `ability_activated` fires when the level line is activated. The line uses the
  stack, so that is before the Class is level 2, and fires even if the Class is
  destroyed in response.
- `counter_placed` needs a level counter, which a Class does not have, and fires
  on every level, so the level-3 purchase would repeat the level-2 ability.

### The shape

- **`EventType.BECAME_LEVEL`** (`became_level`), with `oid`, `card` and `level`,
  fired by `become_level` after the write and only when the level changed.
- **`becomes_level`** in `TRIGGER_EVENTS` and `OBJECT_SUBJECT_TRIGGERS`, and
  **`TriggerSpec.level`** / `TriggerModel.level`, compared in `triggers._matches`
  the way `chapter` is.
- The loader supplies `source: "self"`, requires `level` >= 2 on this event and
  refuses it on any other, and `_check_class_levels` refuses a level no line
  reaches or an ability printed under a higher band than the level it waits for.

### Frontend

Tier D: `describeEvent` reads "<card> becomes level N", and `beatsFor` floats
"Level N" off the Class with the Saga chapter's pulse. Vitest in
`tests/labels.test.ts` and `tests/events.test.ts`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_becomes_level_trigger.py`: the event and its payload; no event
for a level that did not change; nothing while the level line is on the stack
and nothing if the Class is destroyed in response; each rung fires once and only
its own ability; another Class's level does not fire this one; Caretaker's
Talent end to end (the level-2 token copy, the level-1 once-a-turn batched draw
it sets off, no second copy at level 3, the level-3 anthem present only at 3);
and the loader refusals.

## "If the {1}{B} cost was paid" — reading the alternative cost while the spell resolves — 118.9, 707.10

### Overview

Baleful Mastery: "You may pay {1}{B} rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If
the {1}{B} cost was paid, an opponent draws a card. Exile target creature or
planeswalker." Not a documentation gap, though nearly one: `evoke` already *is*
an unconditional alternative mana cost plus the `evoked` condition that reads
which price was paid, and `evoke_label` already renames it on the cast line. What
did not work was the timing. `stack.resolve` wrote `cast_evoked` onto the object
only after `spell_effects`, which was enough for every card that had used it —
each a creature asking from its enters trigger — and meant an `if` inside an
instant's effects read `False` every time. The card would have loaded and been a
strictly better removal spell than the one printed.

### The shape

- `stack._resolve_spell` writes `obj.cast_evoked` before the effects, beside
  `cast_overloaded` and `cast_cost_option`; the later write is unchanged.
- `put_copy_on_stack` copies `evoked` from the original (707.10: a copy copies
  "additional or alternative costs"), so a copied Mastery cast for {1}{B} gives
  out a second card — and a copied Mulldrifter cast for its evoke cost is
  sacrificed too.
- The packet's reference now says `evoke` works on an instant or sorcery and
  that `evoke_label` names an unnamed price (`"paying {1}{B}"`).
- "An opponent draws" is `choose_player` over `each_opponent` then `draw` to the
  binding: one seat, the caster's choice, no prompt with a single opponent.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_alternative_cost_paid.py`: both prices offered, two lands reach
only the cheap one, the line's label, printed mana value; the opponent draws and
the target is exiled on the cheap line and nobody draws on the printed one; at a
three-player table the caster is asked, opponents only, and exactly the chosen
seat draws; a fizzled spell hands out nothing; a copy of the cheap cast draws
again and a copy of the printed cast does not; and the loader still refuses the
rider without the cost and the cost without the rider.

## `from_colors_outside_commander_identity` — protection from each colour your commander lacks — 903.4

### Overview

Commander's Plate: "Equipped creature gets +3/+3 and has protection from each
color that's not in your commander's color identity. Equip commander {3}. Equip
{5}". Everything but the protection was already expressible — `buff` on
`{"attached": true}`, and two equip lines, one whose target selector adds
`is_commander`. The protection static took colours only as a printed list, and
the set here is the five colours *minus* the commanders' identity of whoever
controls the Plate, which is a different list in every deck.

### The shape

- `AbilityModel.from_colors_outside_commander_identity` (bool), carried onto the
  compiled static. The loader counts it as protection's quality, refuses it
  beside `from_colors` and on any effect but `protection`.
- `characteristics.commander_color_identity(state, pid)` — the union of the
  printed `color_identity` of a player's commanders, wherever they are, as colour
  letters.
- `characteristics.protection_from` adds `WUBRG - commander_color_identity(state,
  source.controller)` for a static carrying the flag. Computed at read time, so
  a change of control of the Equipment changes the set; the four rules that read
  protection (damage, enchant/equip, block, target) needed nothing.
- No commander, or a colourless one: protection from all five (903.4).

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_protection_from_colors_outside_commander_identity.py`: mono-black
leaves the other four, partners union, no commander and a colourless commander
are all five, the +3/+3; nothing while unequipped; the commander's zone does not
matter; the Plate's controller decides (handing it over changes the set, stealing
the creature does not) and an opponent's commander is not yours; a red spell
cannot target the equipped creature while a black one can; Equip commander
reaches only the commander and Equip {5} reaches both; and the loader refusals.
## `emblem` — "Target opponent gets an emblem with …" — 114

### Overview

Ob Nixilis Reignited's −8: *"Target opponent gets an emblem with 'Whenever a player
draws a card, you lose 2 life.'"* Ninety-odd catalog cards print an emblem, nearly
all of them planeswalker ultimates, and most of those emblems carry a triggered
ability.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `delayed_trigger` belongs to the ability's controller, so its "you" is the
  player who ultimated, and it carries a duration where an emblem lasts the game.
- `grant_ability` hands an ability to a permanent and ends with it.

### Tier: A, plus a new kind of object

- **`CardModel.emblems`** (`EmblemModel`: `abilities`) compiles, in
  `loader._compile_emblems`, to **`CardDef.emblems`** — a `CardDef` per emblem named
  "<card> Emblem", type line `Emblem`, no types, whose abilities have
  `active_zones` forced to the command zone.
- **`GameObject.emblem`**, an index into the card's `emblems`, and
  **`GameState.card_of`** returns that entry — so the existing command-zone
  trigger walk (Edgar Markov's eminence), `stack.ability_of` and the serializer
  all read the emblem with no change of their own.
- **`primitives.give_emblem`** puts the object straight into the owner's command
  zone (no zone change, so nothing listens) and records
  `EventType.EMBLEM_CREATED`. Not a token, not a commander: no SBA removes it and
  the commander cast walk skips it.
- **`emblem` op** (`ops_player`) with a required `player` spec and `emblem`
  index. The card is read off the new `EffectContext.source_def_id` — the stack
  item's `def_id` — because an ultimate kills its planeswalker before it resolves.
- Loader: `emblem`'s `player` and `emblem` are required; `_check_emblem_references`
  refuses an out-of-range index and an emblem no op gives; `_compile_emblems`
  refuses an empty emblem, a non-triggered ability, any zone but the command zone,
  and `source: "self"`.

### Frontend

State serialization is generic: an emblem arrives in `player_view`'s `command`
list as a card view with its own name, type line and text, and the `/images` map
has no entry for its id. `emblem_created` is narrated — `describeEvent` logs "X
gets an emblem from <card>", and `beatsFor` gives it a neutral banner shaped like
`became_monarch`'s, neutral because an emblem is as often a curse handed to an
opponent as a boon. The command zone holds more than commanders now, so
`zoneGrouping.commandersOf` keeps only `is_commander` cards (an emblem had been
able to become the seat's commander panel, name and art) and the command-pile
badges in `OpponentSeat` and `PlayerOrb` count commanders through
`commandZoneCommanderCount`. **Not built**: a display for emblems — the pile's
viewer lists them, without art.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_emblem.py`: the target opponent gets it in their command zone,
owned and controlled by them, even though the ultimate killed the walker; "you get
an emblem" goes to its controller; it is not a permanent, a token or a commander
and is never offered as a cast; its owner loses 2 on every card anyone draws,
including their own, one trigger per card and per emblem, and given to the
controller it drains the controller instead; it is still there and draining two
turns later; its card view and snapshot; and the loader refusals.

## `wicked_role` — Role tokens, created attached — 303.7a / 704.5y

### Overview

Not Dead After All: *"Until end of turn, target creature you control gains 'When
this creature dies, return it to the battlefield tapped under its owner's control,
then create a Wicked Role token attached to it.'"* The pool had no Role and no
Aura token of any kind; thirty-five catalog cards make Roles.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- There was no token to create.
- `create_token` then `attach` makes a Role even when the host is gone; the token
  arrives unattached, 704.5m bins it, and a Wicked Role drains every opponent. The
  Role rulings say it is not created.
- Nothing implemented the Role rule.

### The shape

- **`wicked_role`** in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json`: Enchantment — Aura Role,
  "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1" (`buff` on `attached`) and "When this Aura is
  put into a graveyard from the battlefield, each opponent loses 1 life" (`dies`,
  `source: self`).
- **`create_token`'s `attached_to`**: resolves the host first and creates nothing
  if none is on the battlefield; otherwise attaches each Aura it made, in creation
  order.
- **`GameObject.attached_timestamp`**, stamped by `primitives.attach` from the
  new `GameState.alloc_timestamp` (613.7e).
- **`sba._role_rule`** (704.5y): groups Roles by host and controller and puts all
  but the newest into the graveyard.
- Loader: `attached_to` only on `create_token`, validated as a selector, and only
  naming an Aura token (`validate_token_references`). That check now also walks
  `grantable_abilities`, which it never did — a granted ability naming an unknown
  token loaded clean and crashed mid-game.

### Frontend

None. An Aura token is an ordinary attached permanent to the serializer.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_wicked_role.py`: the token's types; created attached, +1/+1;
drains when destroyed and when it falls off a dead creature; nothing created (and
nothing drained) when the host is gone; your Role on an opponent's creature; a
second Role replaces the first and the replaced Wicked Role drains; different
players' Roles and different creatures' Roles coexist; newest by attachment, not
arrival; Not Dead After All end to end (returns tapped wearing the Role, no drain;
without it the creature stays dead; the grant is gone next turn); and the loader
refusals, including an unknown token in a granted ability.
## `lose_life` `as` — "the life lost this way"

### Overview

Gray Merchant of Asphodel: "each opponent loses X life, where X is your devotion
to black. You gain life equal to the life lost this way." The second sentence
reads the life the first one actually took, after replacements.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `primitives.lose_life` already returned the actual loss, but `op_lose_life`
  discarded it, so nothing could read it.
- Recomputing the amount in `gain_life` (Malakir Bloodwitch's shipped answer)
  gains X against a Bloodletter-doubled 2X and against a locked 0.
- `life_lost_this_turn` is the turn ledger, not this effect's loss.

### The shape

- `lose_life` joins `RECORDING_OPS`; `as` binds an int, the sum over every player
  hit, overwriting any earlier value of that name.
- The loader's existing `as` guard now accepts it on `lose_life`.
- Malakir Bloodwitch's answer is rewritten onto the binding, so it is exact under
  a replacement too.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_life_lost_this_way.py`: the sum across two opponents, an int,
zero, no `as` writes nothing, overwrite rather than accumulate, a doubled loss
gains the doubled amount, a locked opponent contributes nothing, and the loader.

## Extort — 702.101

### Overview

"Whenever you cast a spell, you may pay {W/B}. If you do, each opponent loses 1
life and you gain that much life." Nineteen catalog cards print it; Crypt Ghast
filed it as blocked.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

Every piece existed except "that much life": counting opponents is wrong under a
loss doubler. The previous commit's `lose_life` `as` binding is that read, so
extort needs no engine change and no `Keyword`.

### The shape

- `templates.extort_ability(text)`: a `spell_cast` trigger (controller you), a
  `may` with `pay: {"mana": "{W/B}"}`, then `lose_life` each opponent 1 `as`
  `extorted` and `gain_life` of the binding.
- The `extort` template writes it for a bare "Extort" line. Syndic of Tithes,
  Basilica Guards, Tithe Drinker, Knight of Obligation, Kingpin's Pet,
  Syndicate Enforcer and Basilica Screecher now translate and pass all six gates.
- `docs/keywords.md`'s row names the binding and the template.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_extort.py`, against `t_extortioner` (pinned equal to the
template's output): paying drains and gains, two opponents gain two, white pays
the hybrid pip, the mana is really taken, declining does nothing, a player who
cannot pay is not asked, two instances trigger twice, an opponent's spell does
not trigger it, and a doubled loss gains double.

## `add_mana_on_tap` — "Whenever you tap a Swamp for mana, add an additional {B}"

### Overview

Crypt Ghast's second line: a triggered mana ability (605.1b). It resolves right
after the mana ability that triggered it, without the stack (605.4a). The same
sentence is printed on Nirkana Revenant, Nissa, Who Shakes the World, Vernal
Bloom, Gauntlet of Might and Leyline of Abundance.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `double_land_mana` (Vorinclex) is a bare boolean: no filter on what was
  tapped, and it doubles what the land made instead of adding a fixed {B}.
- A `triggered` ability cannot fire inside cost payment, where nothing may be
  queued or asked, and there is no tapped-for-mana trigger event.
- Nothing in the engine already did this, so it was not a documentation gap.

### The shape

- A player-wide static `add_mana_on_tap` with `affects_player`,
  `tapped_permanent` (`types`/`subtypes`/`supertypes`, the new
  `loader.TAPPED_PERMANENT_KEYS`) and `add_mana`.
- `player_statics.mana_added_on_tap` returns `(source, mana)` per applicable
  static, through `_active_player_statics`, so a `condition` is honoured.
- It is read in `costs._sources_of` (planner), `costs.activate_mana_ability`
  (the pool, tagged with the static's source, only for abilities with {T}) and
  legality's chip label, all through `mana_added_total`/`plus_mana`.
- Crypt Ghast is authored with the extort template's ability and this static.
- The golden vocabulary is re-pinned for the new effect and key set.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_add_mana_on_tap.py`: a Swamp makes two, a Forest one, no Ghast
one, two Ghasts three, the extra pip tagged with the Ghast, an opponent's Swamp
unaffected by `you`, `any` paying the tapper, a land made a Swamp counting, the
solver paying {B}{B}{B}{B} from two Swamps (and not without), legality offering
the spell (and not without), the effect ending with its source, the condition
asked, and the loader refusals.
was no replacement of life *gain* here; that is `replace_life_gain`, below.

## `replace_life_gain` — "you gain twice that much life instead"

### Overview

Alhammarret's Archive: *"If you would gain life, you gain **twice that much life
instead**."* Its second line, the draw doubler with Bard's exemption, already
shipped as `replace_draw`; this was the half that kept the card out of the
Sheoldred, the Apocalypse deck.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `replace_life_loss` multiplies losses only.
- A `you_gain_life` trigger with a `gain_life` effect is a second gain: it uses
  the stack, fires `LIFE_GAINED` a second time for every life-gain trigger on the
  board, and re-triggers itself.

### The shape

- **`replace_life_gain`**, a player-wide static (`affects_player`,
  `gain_multiplier`, optional `condition`), read by
  `player_statics.life_gain_multiplier` through `_active_player_statics`.
- **One call site**, `primitives.gain_life`, the only place a life total goes up.
  Lifelink reaches it through `_apply_lifelink`, so lifelink is doubled and the
  damage is not.
- `gain_life` now returns, and `LIFE_GAINED` now carries, the replaced amount.
- The life lock (118.5) is checked before the multiplier.
- The loader requires `gain_multiplier`, refuses it below 2 and on any other
  effect, and refuses `affects`/`amount` beside it.

### Divergences

Two doublers multiply (614.5); 616.1's ordering is not asked, which for a
product cannot show.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_life_gain_replacement.py`: the multiplier (controller only,
`affects_player: "opponent"`, two doublers, the condition read), the gain and its
return value, one event carrying 6, zero and a locked total, the Archive leaving,
lifelink doubled without doubling the damage, a real cast spell, and the loader
refusals. Alhammarret's Archive is authored whole.

## `cant_gain_life` — "Your opponents can't gain life"

### Overview

Erebos, God of the Dead's third line. Its devotion clause (`set_types` under a
`mana_symbols` condition) and its `{1}{B}, Pay 2 life: Draw a card` were already
expressible; this was the line that kept the card blocked.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

- `lock_life_total` is a one-shot op with a fixed duration that stops losses as
  well as gains, and does not follow a permanent staying on the battlefield.
- `replace_life_gain` with a multiplier of 0 is refused, and would still be a
  replacement that another replacement could reorder.

### The shape

- **`cant_gain_life`**, a player-wide static (`affects_player`, optional
  `condition`), read by `player_statics.player_cant_gain_life`.
- **One call site**, `primitives.gain_life`, after the life lock and **before**
  `life_gain_multiplier`. Nothing moves and no `LIFE_GAINED` fires, so
  life-gain triggers stay silent.
- The loader refuses `affects` and `amount` beside it.

### How it composes with `replace_life_gain`

"Can't" wins (101.2). Checked first, so an opponent's Archive under Erebos gains
nothing, and the Archive's own controller (who Erebos does not name) still
gains double.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_cant_gain_life.py`: who it names, `affects_player` both ways,
the op and lifelink stopped (lifelink's damage still dealt), no event and no
trigger, the lift when the source leaves, the condition read, the composition
with a doubler on either side, and the loader refusals. Erebos, God of the Dead
is authored whole.

## `life_gained_this_turn` — "if you gained life this turn"

### Overview

Witch of the Moors: *"At the beginning of your end step, **if you gained life this
turn**, each opponent sacrifices a creature of their choice and you return up to
one target creature card from your graveyard to your hand."* The rest of the
sentence (`for_each_player` over a `sacrifice` with the player's own choice, and
an optional graveyard target) was already expressible.

### Not a documentation gap

The ledger had `life_lost`, `damage_taken` and the draw count, and nothing in the
engine recorded a gain at all, so this was real work rather than a missing line
in the packet.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

A `has_turn_flag` set by a `you_gain_life` trigger on the Witch is an ability the
card does not print, and it misses a gain made before the Witch entered.

### The shape

- **`TurnLedger.life_gained`**, cleared with the ledger at cleanup.
- Folded in `GameState.emit` off `LIFE_GAINED`, beside `life_lost`: every gain
  counts (the op, lifelink), with the amount the event carries (doubled under
  `replace_life_gain`), and a gain that did not happen fires no event.
- **`{"life_gained_this_turn": <player spec>}`**, a value leaf; "if you gained
  life" is a `cmp` `>` 0 on the trigger's `condition`, re-read on resolution.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_life_gained_this_turn.py`: the fold, accumulation, lifelink, a
loss that is not a gain, gain-then-loss, per player, zero, a locked total and
`cant_gain_life` not counting, the condition, the refusal of an unknown
spelling, an end-step trigger against a real turn with and without a gain and
with a gain made before the permanent entered, and the tally gone next turn.
Witch of the Moors is authored whole.

## `half` — "half …, round up" — 107.1a

### Overview

Peer into the Abyss: *"Target player draws cards equal to **half** the number of
cards in their library and loses **half** their life. **Round up** each time."*

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

`value_keys` had `sum`, `minus`, `times`, `max` and `min` — no division and no
rounding — so ceil(n/2) could not be built. `count` and `life_of` already read
the library and the life total; only the halving was missing.

### The shape

- **`{"half": {"of": <value>, "round": "up" | "down"}}`** in `values.VALUE_KEYS`,
  evaluated with floor division (negated around it for the ceiling).
- **`validate_half`**: `of` required, `round` required and one of
  `HALF_ROUNDING`, no other keys. A default direction is refused because both are
  printed (107.1a), and the wrong one is invisible on every even number.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_half_rounded.py`: Peer end to end on odd and even libraries and
life totals, one life (lost entirely), an empty library (still costs life); both
directions over 0, 1, 2, 7, 40 and a negative; composition inside and around
`sum`; and every loader refusal.


## `any_order` — "on the bottom of their library in any order" — 401.4

### Overview

Teferi's Puzzle Box: *"At the beginning of each player's draw step, that player
puts the cards in their hand on the bottom of their library **in any order**, then
draws that many cards."* The first half of the sentence.

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

`put_on_top` with `bottom: true` resolved its selector through `choose_objects`,
which for `count: "all"` returns the pool in hand order and moves each card with
no question. `scry` and `look_at_top` order only cards taken off the top of the
library, never cards from a hand.

### The shape

- **`any_order: true`** on `put_on_top`, read by `ops_cards._in_owners_order`:
  per owner, `ask_objects` with a count of one over the cards left, purpose
  `library_order`, until one remains. No new `DecisionKind`.
- Each answer is the next card put there: the last chosen is the bottom card on
  the bottom and the top card on top.
- The loader refuses it on any other op, as a non-boolean, and beside `from_top`
  or `owner_chooses`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_put_on_bottom_any_order.py`: the same hand under in two orders,
the top of the library undisturbed, the top-of-library reading, one question per
card but the last, the owner asked when the hand is an opponent's, one card and
an empty hand asking nothing, and the loader refusals.


## `put_on_top`'s `as` — "then draws that many cards"

### Overview

The second half of Teferi's Puzzle Box: *"…puts the cards in their hand on the
bottom of their library in any order, **then draws that many cards**."*

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

`put_on_top` carried no `as`, and the loader refuses an `as` on an op that
records nothing. `cards_in_hand` read after the tuck is 0; `snapshot` captures one
object, not a count; a per-card `for_each` interleaves the draws with the tucks.

### The shape

- **`put_on_top` in `RECORDING_OPS`**, binding the list of oids that
  `move_object` actually left in a library — not those chosen.
- Assigned, not accumulated, and written even when empty.
- Read with the existing `{"count": {"binding": …}}`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_count_moved_cards.py`: a Puzzle Box test card on its owner's
first draw step (no draw, 103.8a) with three, one and no cards in hand — the hand
comes back the same size, off the top, with the old hand underneath; the binding
names what arrived; a second tuck of nothing leaves an empty binding rather than
a stale one; the loader accepts the key.


## `may`'s `x` — "you may pay {X}, where X is less than or equal to…"

### Overview

Well of Lost Dreams: *"Whenever you gain life, you may pay {X}, where X is less
than or equal to the amount of life you gained. If you do, draw X cards."*

### Why the existing vocabulary would not do

`may`'s `pay` charges a fixed cost, and `pay.times` scales it by a number the card
computes — X equal to the gain, never less. `choose_x` was asked only by
`game.py` at cast and activation time. `may` with `repeat` around {1} and one
draw interleaves payments with draws and has no ceiling.

### The shape

- **`x: {"max": <value>, "as": <name>, "prompt"?}`** on `may`, beside a `pay`
  whose mana carries `{X}`.
- `ops_control._announce_x`: after the yes, `ask_x` over 0 up to
  min(`max`, `max_affordable_x` of the player's pool and sources), then `pay`
  with that `x`, then the paid X bound under `as` before the effects run.
- The loader (`_validate_pay_x`) requires `max` and `as`, refuses an `{X}` with
  no `x` and an `x` with no `{X}`, `x` anywhere but a paying `may`, and `x`
  beside `repeat`, `pay.times` or `pay.mana_reduction`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_pay_x_on_resolution.py`: the ceiling is the life gained with
plenty of mana and the mana with plenty of life; nothing open charges {0} without
asking; X paid is X drawn and X tapped; a smaller X than the gain; X = 0; declining
asks no X; and the loader refusals.
### One narrowing, recorded -- and since lifted
A Phyrexian pip in an **activated ability's** cost had to be paid with mana,
because the choice was offered only as a cast line. Lifted by
`black_mana_as_phyrexian` below, which needed the choice in every cost.
## `black_mana_as_phyrexian` — K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth's "for each {B} in a cost"

### Overview

*"For each {B} in a cost, you may pay 2 life rather than pay that mana."* The
line the Sheoldred deck's K'rrik is played for. The gap record named it; no
existing static could say it — `pay_life_instead` pays a whole spell's mana value
off the top of the library, and `spell_cost_reduction` can only shrink generic
mana.

### The shape

- **The static.** `black_mana_as_phyrexian`, player-wide (`affects_player`),
  read by `player_statics.player_pays_life_for_black`.
- **The cost.** `ManaCost.black_as_phyrexian` turns each `{B}` into a `{B/P}` and
  gives every black hybrid pip (`{B/R}`, `{2/B}`) a life half, which is the
  ruling: "if you choose to pay {B} this way, K'rrik's ability allows you to pay
  life". Mana value, colours, chroma and `text` do not move.
- **Spells** reuse the Phyrexian cast lines untouched: `_cast_variant` and
  `Game._cast` convert the variant's price before counting / buying pips.
  `paying_phyrexian` now buys single-symbol pips first, so a `{B}` is bought
  before a `{B/R}` beside it.
- **Every other cost** asks. `costs.life_for_mana_range` returns the fewest pips
  that must be bought for the remainder to be payable and the most the life total
  can buy (less any life the cost itself charges; none under a life lock);
  `can_pay` / `can_pay_mana` offer the cost when that range exists, and `pay` asks
  `CHOOSE_MODE` only when it holds more than one number. X ceilings on
  activations are measured with every buyable pip bought
  (`costs.most_life_for_mana`). The cast line passes `life_for_mana=False`.

That second half is also what lifts the recorded narrowing on printed Phyrexian
pips in activated abilities (Birthing Pod's `{1}{G/P}`): same code, no K'rrik
needed.

### Not modelled

Two different life-payable pips in one cost (`{2/B}` beside `{B/R}`) are bought
in a fixed order rather than asked; a strive surcharge's `{B}` is paid with mana.
No shipped card prints either. In `docs/rules-coverage.md`.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_black_mana_as_phyrexian.py`: the conversion (plain, hybrid,
`{2/B}`, already-Phyrexian, untouched generic and other colours, the buying
order); the cast lines with and without black sources, without K'rrik, under an
opponent's K'rrik, a hybrid spell, a spell with no black; the 118.4 boundary;
what a cast charges; activations offered off no mana, withheld without K'rrik or
the life, the forced answer not asked, the real choice asked and honoured, the
X ceiling; and a printed `{G/P}` activation payable with life. K'rrik, Son of
Yawgmoth is authored.

## `playable: "while_exiled"` — "for as long as they remain exiled"

### Overview

Elder Brain: *"You may play lands and cast spells from among the exiled cards for
as long as they remain exiled."* The four durations the engine had either end
(`this_turn`, `your_next_end_step`, `end_of_your_next_turn`) or forbid the turn
of the grant (`later_turns`, Plot) -- and Elder Brain's cards are playable in the
second main phase of the very combat that exiled them.

### The shape

- **`while_exiled`** in `PLAYABLE_DURATIONS`. `playable_live` already answers
  True for a duration it has no clock for, and no hook in `turn` names it, so the
  permission stands until the zone-change reset clears it.
- **Loader.** Accepted on `exile`, on `look_at_top` into exile, and on
  `grant_playable` whose selector reads `zone: "exile"`; refused elsewhere.
- **Every seat's exile for a land drop.** `legality._land_actions` walked only
  the player's own exile, so a land exiled out of an opponent's hand was never
  offered -- the cast side (`casting._cast_actions`) already walked every seat.
  `Game._play_land` now sets the land's controller to the player making the drop
  before it moves, so it enters under their control (110.2) and not its owner's.
- **Packet.** `reference()["playable_durations"]` lists the values, which no
  worker could see before.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_playable_while_exiled.py`: live on the turn of the grant, on the
next turn and the one after; untouched by every expiry hook; gone once the card
leaves exile and comes back, and used up by playing it; an opponent's exiled land
offered and entering under your control; the loader's accept and refuse cases;
and the packet listing.

## `any_color` — "spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast it"

### Overview

Elder Brain's last sentence, and the half of it that makes the stolen hand usable.
Not a documentation gap: no shipped card printed it, and `grant_playable`'s
`any_type` (Valigarmanda) is a different, broader sentence -- "any type" lets
coloured mana pay `{C}`, and "any color" does not.

The gap record claimed colourless mana could still pay only generic; the ruling
is the other way (Mycosynth Lattice: colourless mana may be spent as though it
had a colour), and the implementation follows the ruling.

### The shape

- **`ManaCost.as_any_color`**: `{W}`-`{G}` and every hybrid / remaining Phyrexian
  pip fold into one generic each; `{C}` and `X` stay; `text` is the printed cost.
- **`GameObject.playable_any_color`**, written by `exile`, `look_at_top` and
  `grant_playable` from `any_color`, cleared wherever `playable_any_type` is
  (the zone-change reset and `turn._expire_permissions`).
- **Priced and paid** in `_cast_variant` / `_priced_tuples` and `Game._cast`,
  beside the any-type waiver and under the same `playable_live` gate.
- **Loader**: needs a permission to ride on; refused beside `any_type`.

K'rrik's Phyrexian conversion runs first, so a black pip bought with life leaves
the cost before the colours are waived.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_spend_mana_as_any_color.py`: the cost conversion (colours fold,
`{C}` stays, a hybrid pip is one, X and the printed cost survive); a stolen
`{B}{B}` spell castable off Plains, paid and resolved into its owner's
graveyard; the strict counterfactual; hybrid pips at one each; the caster's own
spells untouched; the flag leaving with the permission; a Sol Ring paying
`{B}{B}`; `{C}` not waived; and the loader cases. Elder Brain is authored.

## `any_number_in_deck` — "A deck can have any number of cards named …"

### Overview

Rule 903.5b says a Commander deck may contain only one of any card with a
particular English name **other than basic lands**, and then adds "unless that
card's text says otherwise". Only the basic-land half was read, so a deck built
on twenty Persistent Petitioners — a legal deck, and an archetype — failed
construction outright and could not be imported at all.

### The shape

- **`CardDef.any_number_in_deck`** parses the printed sentence and matches the
  name inside it against the card's **own** name, so Shadowborn Apostle does not
  license a playset of Relentless Rats and a card that merely quotes another's
  line receives nothing.
- **`validate_deck`** asks it beside `is_basic`; `tests/cards/test_deck_legality.py`
  asks the same predicate rather than its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
- **`verify._covered`** grows one claimant for the line, and this is the half
  that actually kept the card out of the pool. The sentence is a
  *deck-construction* rule read while a deck is built, so once the card is an
  object in a game there is nothing left for it to do and no ability can
  honestly carry it — an `AbilityModel` is activated, triggered or static, and
  this is none of the three. Petitioners failed gate 3 with both of its real
  lines implemented and verified. The claimant is strict for `bestow`'s and
  `devoid`'s reason: gated on `any_number_in_deck`, so the words cannot be
  claimed without the rule standing behind them.

### Superseded by

`deck_copy_limit`, below, which reads the bounded form of the same sentence.
Nazgûl's "A deck can have **up to nine** cards named Nazgûl" was left unmatched
here, keeping the one-copy default — the safe direction for a construction check
to be incomplete in, and a legal deck refused.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_deck_copy_limits.py`: twenty Petitioners legal and the same
deck with an ordinary card still singleton; the sentence matched against the
card's own name; basic lands exempt by the rule with no sentence to read; and
the claimant scoped to its own line. Persistent Petitioners is authored.

## `skip_untap_step` — "doesn't untap during their controllers' untap steps"

### Overview

Back to Basics, Intruder Alarm, Winter Orb, Mana Vault. `static_effects` carried
`untap_during_each_untap_step` — the exact inverse, which *adds* untaps — and
nothing that suppressed one. 145 catalog cards were waiting on it.

### The shape

- **`player_statics.untap_held(state, active_pid)`** returns the oids held down,
  written directly beside its inverse `untap_also` and read in the same place
  for the same reason: whether a permanent untaps is a fact about a *set* of
  permanents at one moment in the turn, and no characteristic carries it.
- **`primitives.untap_all`** consults it once per step rather than once per
  permanent — Intruder Alarm on a full board would otherwise make the untap step
  quadratic.
- **`not_supertypes`** joins the static filter language so Back to Basics can say
  "**nonbasic** lands". The negation of `supertypes`, added for `not_keywords`'
  stated reason: the effect-side selector language always had it and the static
  one did not. A `not_types` complement is not a spelling of it — that is every
  permanent which is not a land, the opposite set.

### Why not the two fields that already suppressed untapping

Both are written by resolution rather than printed on a card. `skip_next_untap`
is a one-shot that `untap_all` spends in the very untap step it skips, so it
holds Mana Vault for one turn and releases it on the next; `frozen_by` is set by
the `freeze` op. Both are ops, so the only route from a printed static was to
invent a `self_enters` trigger for a line that is printed as a static — which
would sit on the stack, be respondable, and reinstall on every re-entry.

### The three things that would each be a different card

- **Any controller.** Both enchantments say "their controllers' untap steps".
  `affects` may name `controller: "any"`, as `cant_attack` already does. Intruder
  Alarm locking only its own side would be a one-sided card rather than the
  symmetric drawback it is built around.
- **It must not spend `skip_next_untap`.** `untap_all` checks the held set
  *first*, so a static already covering a permanent does not burn somebody
  else's one-shot.
- **Explicit untaps still work.** Read by the untap step alone, so Mana Vault's
  upkeep payment untaps it and Intruder Alarm's own "untap all creatures"
  trigger — the card's entire engine — is unaffected.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_skip_untap_step.py`: the self-lock and its counterfactual; an
explicit untap still working; the hold ending when the source leaves; an
opponent's creature held on their own untap step, with the pair that makes it
mean something; the `not_supertypes` clause, where a basic land must *not* be
held; and both halves of the `skip_next_untap` interaction.

## `replace_mill` — "they mill twice that many cards instead"

### Overview

Bruvac the Grandiloquent, Fraying Sanity. `static_effects` carried the whole
`replace_*` family — `replace_draw`, `replace_life_gain`, `replace_life_loss`,
`replace_token_creation` — and no mill member. `mill` existed only as an effect
op and as a cost: as something *this card's controller does*, never as an event
that could be replaced.

### The shape

A player-wide static (`affects_player`, no `affects`) with a required
`mill_multiplier` of 2 or more, applied in **`primitives.mill_cards`**.

That placement is the capability. `mill_cards` is the one choke point every mill
goes through — the `mill` op, the `mill` cost, and dredge (702.52a) — so Bruvac
doubles the mills an *opponent's own* cards cause, which is the entire card. A
doubling written into `op_mill` would only ever see mills its own controller
caused, and Bruvac's controller is not the one being milled.

### Why it is not shaped like `replace_draw`

`draw_replacements` returns `(source, multiplier)` pairs and
`replacements._draw_one` recurses per card with an `applied` set, because 121.2
makes drawing N cards **N separate draws** and the "except the first one you draw
in each of your draw steps" exemption moves between them.

701.13a makes milling N cards **one event**. So `mill_multiplier` returns a
single factor, the mill is replaced once in place by multiplying its count, and
there is no per-card recursion for 614.5 to guard against. Two doublers are two
different replacements applying to the same event and compound (616.1) to four —
the product across sources, each visited once.

### Not modelled

A `mill` trigger event, which is the tempting approximation and a different
card: it would fire after the cards were already in the graveyard and mill again
*alongside* rather than *instead*, parting company from the printed card the
moment anything cares how many cards were milled at once, or the library runs
short.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_replace_mill.py`: an opponent milling double with its
counterfactual; the controller **not** doubled (the near miss a player-agnostic
implementation passes silently); `affects_player: "you"` for Fraying Sanity's
half; two doublers compounding to 4×; a mill of zero not being an event;
701.13b's short library milling what is there rather than over-counting; the
hold ending when the source leaves; and the load-time guards.

## `replace_empty_draw` — "you win the game instead"

### Overview

Jace, Wielder of Mysteries; Laboratory Maniac. The draw-replacement family had
one member, `replace_draw`, and it is a pure multiplier — the loader requires
`draw_multiplier` and refuses anything below 2, so no key on it can name a
different outcome. This is also the one branch that static can never reach:
there is no card to multiply when the library is empty.

### The shape

A player-wide static with no parameters (`affects_player`, and the loader
refuses `affects` and `amount` — the replacement has no size), read in
`replacements._draw_one`.

**It replaces the draw rather than reacting to it**, and that is the whole
design. `primitives.draw_cards` treats an empty library as an *attempt*: it sets
the 104.3c "will lose" flag and fires no `DRAW` event at all. A trigger would
therefore fail twice over — nothing to fire on, and the state-based action would
eliminate the player at the next check regardless, which comes before anything a
trigger could do. Replacing means `draw_cards` is never called and the flag is
never set.

**Checked before the doublers.** A `replace_draw` turns one draw into two, each
offered this replacement in turn, so an empty library wins on the first of them
rather than after both have tried and failed.

The win goes through `sba.declare_win`, which eliminates every *other* player
and lets `check_game_over` draw its own conclusion (104.2a). The engine has one
writer of a game result and this is not a second one.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_replace_empty_draw.py`: the win, and the ordinary 104.3c loss
without the static; the "will lose" flag never being set; a non-empty library
drawing as usual; the win landing on the draw that empties the library; an
opponent decking being unaffected (the near miss a player-agnostic
implementation passes silently); the permission ending with its source; and the
load-time guards.

## `shares_permanent_type_with` — "shares a permanent type with it"

### Overview

Cloudstone Curio. The selector language had two dynamic "shares a … with"
clauses — `shares_a_type_with` (subtypes) and `shares_a_color_with` (colours) —
and no card-type member.

### The shape

A selector key taking a binding name, intersecting **`types`** where its sibling
intersects `subtypes`. Read from derived characteristics on both sides.

A separate key rather than a mode of the subtype one, because the wrong reading
is *quietly narrower*: written with `shares_a_type_with`, Cloudstone Curio finds
another Goblin when a Goblin enters and **nothing at all** when a land, a
typeless artifact, or any permanent without shared creature types enters. That
card loads clean, prints the right sentence and does a fraction of it.

A literal `types` list cannot stand in: which permanent type matters is decided
at resolution by whatever just entered.

An intersection, so an artifact creature reaches both the artifacts and the
creatures (205.2a). Both objects are on the battlefield, where every card type
is a permanent type (110.4a), so no spell type can appear on either side.

The printed **"another"** is `exclude_binding`, not this clause — a permanent
shares a type with itself, and without the exclusion the card bounces whatever
just entered.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_shares_permanent_type.py`: a creature finding creatures and not
lands; a land finding a land, which is exactly the case the subtype reading gets
wrong; two creatures with no shared subtype still matching, with a fixture-sanity
assertion so the test cannot go vacuous; an artifact creature reaching both pools
and a plain creature not reaching the artifacts; the self-match and its
exclusion; and an unbound name failing closed.

## `"any"` — "spend this mana only to activate abilities"

### Overview

Cryptic Trilobite; Omen Hawker. `mana_restriction` already carried the
cast/activate split Secluded Courtyard needed, but every group either half could
hold was a set of literal card type or subtype **names**:
`RestrictionGroup.satisfied_by` asks `required <= names`, where `names` is the
types and subtypes of the source whose ability is being activated. This line
names no type at all, and there is no name that every source has — so nothing in
the language could mean it.

### The shape

`"any"` in place of a half's list of groups, compiling to a single **empty**
`RestrictionGroup` — satisfied for every purpose of that kind, nothing being
required.

**The restriction lives in the other half.** With no `cast` groups the mana can
never pay for a spell, and `ManaRestriction` already documented an empty tuple as
"never". That is the whole of what the printed line forbids, which is why the
wildcard is not the same thing as no restriction.

**Refused on both halves at once**, which is ordinary mana wearing a restriction,
and **refused bare**: a bare restriction is the `cast` half, so a bare `"any"`
would be mana that pays for every spell ever printed and merely declines to
activate an ability — one keystroke from the line that was meant, and silent.

A word rather than an accepted empty list. `[]` stays a load error, because a
blank is what a mistake looks like and reading it as "everything" is how a
strictly better card ships quietly.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_mana_restriction_activate_any.py`: the empty group funding an
Enchantment, a Land and a Creature sink with the same `{2}` ability — three type
lines sharing no literal name, which is the argument that no enumeration could
have stood in — and the empty name set, which no enumeration reaches at all; the
mana refusing every spell, which is the printed restriction; the payment actually
happening and the font actually tapping; the solver's three answers from
`mana_sources`, against `t_unrestricted_font` as the control; the mirror
`{"cast": "any"}`; and the three load-time guards.

`t_unrestricted_font` is kept as a live card because it is the strictly better
card this closes — the spelling shipped Omen Hawker and Automated Artificer use
today, which casts spells their printed lines forbid.

## `cast_as_though_flash` — "any player may cast spells as though they had flash"

### Overview

Tidal Barracuda; Leyline of Anticipation and Vedalken Orrery with
`affects_player: "you"`. The permissive twin of `cant_cast_spells`, and the first
static in the engine that widens a **timing** window rather than a zone one.

### The shape

A player-wide static taking `affects_player` ("you" / "opponent" / "any") and an
optional `condition`, and no `affects` or `amount` — both are load errors, for
the same reason its twin refuses them: "you may cast **Spirit** spells as though
they had flash" written with a filter would load clean and hand the permission to
every spell.

**The seam is `casting._timing_ok`.** It read

    if card.is_instant or Keyword.FLASH.value in card.keywords: return True
    return sorcery_speed

— printed characteristics and the window, with no `state` and no `pid`, so
nothing a permanent did could be consulted from it. That is the block three gap
records recorded. It now takes both.

**Widened there rather than at one cast path**, because every zone a spell can be
cast from asks that same function: hand, graveyard (flashback, retrace), exile
(foretell, adventure, plot), a Bolas's Citadel top, and a second face. Twelve call
sites, one answer. A permission written into the hand loop would pass every
obvious test and leave the other six at sorcery speed.

**It permits and never compels.** 101.2 still gives a "can't" the last word, so a
seat under `cant_cast_spells` casts nothing — which is the pairing Tidal Barracuda
prints on one card, and the reason that card is the right witness.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_cast_as_though_flash.py`: the sorcery-speed baseline as a control
on both sides (a plain sorcery off-turn, an instant either way); the permission
lifting the window for a sorcery and a creature spell, on the opponent's turn and
in a non-main step; the wearing-off when the source leaves; `affects_player`
separating "you" from "any", in both directions, with the predicate and the action
list asserted together; the `condition` honoured and un-honoured; the prohibition
outranking the permission, against the un-locked control; a *granted* `flash`
keyword still not doing it, which is the near miss; and the three load-time guards.

### Not done

The turn-scoped op form — "you may cast spells this turn as though they had flash"
(Borne Upon a Wind, Emergence Zone) — which writes this same permission with a
turn on it. A second capability and a second run; neither card is in the deck this
was built for.

## `activate_loyalty_as_though_instant` — Teferi's timing line

### Overview

Teferi, Master of Time: "You may activate loyalty abilities of Teferi on any
player's turn any time you could cast an instant."

### The shape

A static taking `affects` — whose loyalty abilities are freed, in the ordinary
permanent-filter language, where `{"self_only": true}` is the printed "of Teferi"
— and an optional `condition`. No `affects_player` and no `amount`; both are load
errors. `affects` is **required** rather than defaulted to self, because a missing
filter matches every permanent and would hand the whole table instant-speed
loyalty in silence.

**It could not be an ability key.** The loader forces sorcery speed on for every
loyalty ability:

    sorcery_speed_only = model.sorcery_speed_only or (cost is not None and cost.loyalty is not None)

so `sorcery_speed_only: false` written on the card is swallowed by the `or`. There
is no spelling that reaches the flag, which is why the permission arrives from the
board instead.

**606.3 is two rules and this lifts one of them.** The window moves; the
one-loyalty-ability-per-permanent-per-turn limit is a separate check in
`_ability_aims` and stands. A waiver written as "skip the 606.3 check" rather than
"skip the timing check" passes every obvious test and quietly turns one
planeswalker into three cards a turn.

**A different door from `cast_as_though_flash`.** That static widens the *casting*
window for spells; this one the *activation* window for abilities. Closing either
leaves the other shut, and neither leaks into the other.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_activate_loyalty_as_though_instant.py`: the sorcery-speed
baseline on a walker without the line (off-turn and off-main-phase); the
permission lifting both halves of the window, together and separately; the
once-per-turn limit still biting, on your turn and theirs; a non-loyalty
sorcery-speed ability on the same permanent staying refused; the `affects` filter
actually read — an "orrery" form reaching another permanent's walker, and Teferi's
`self_only` form not reaching its neighbour — plus the wearing-off; the two
timing permissions not leaking into one another in either direction; and the four
load-time guards.

### Not done

Leonin Shikari's "you may activate equip abilities any time you could cast an
instant" — the same seam pointed at equip. Nothing on `Ability` marks an equip
ability, so it stays a gap rather than becoming a word that half means it.

## `once_this_turn` — "the next spell you cast this turn"

### Overview

Sea Gate Stormcaller. A third value for a delayed trigger's `duration`, and the
one :data:`DELAYED_DURATIONS` had already described in the negative:

> The two axes — repeating-or-once, and turn-scoped-or-not — happen to be
> correlated in both printed cards … a card that separated them would need a
> third entry here rather than a different reading of these two. That card does
> not exist in the pool; when it does, this is where it goes.

### The shape

Fires **once**, like `until_it_fires`, and expires at cleanup, like `this_turn`.
One line of engine: `triggers._arm_delayed` strikes it off as it arms, beside
`until_it_fires`. The expiry needed nothing — `turn._cleanup_step` keeps only
`until_it_fires`, so anything else is dropped whether or not it ever fired.

Both existing values are wrong on exactly one axis, and both were **measured in a
real game** rather than reasoned about:

- `this_turn` re-arms on every matching spell. A kicked Stormcaller copied a
  second Night's Whisper twice as well — that is a Thousand-Year Storm.
- `until_it_fires` outlives the turn, because `_cleanup_step`'s retention clause
  was written for Palace Jailer, whose crown may not move for six turns. A
  Stormcaller whose controller casts nothing cheap copies a spell on a later turn.

Latching `this_turn` by hand is not a substitute either: `set_turn_flag`'s
`objects` go through `resolve_pool`, whose `self_only` finds the source only while
it is on the battlefield, so the latch stops the moment the 2/1 dies and the card
copies every cheap spell for the rest of the turn.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_delayed_once_this_turn.py`: one firing and not a second; the
subscription actually struck off the state rather than ignored afterwards; an
unfired subscription gone by the next turn, and a later spell not firing it; both
near misses kept as live cards and measured as controls (`this_turn` gaining twice,
`until_it_fires` gaining on a later turn); the condition-as-filter discriminating in
both directions, including that a passed-over spell does **not** spend the
subscription; and the load-time guards, the misspelling among them — a typo falling
through to the `this_turn` default would silently retime the card.

### Not done

A `filter` on a delayed trigger's `trigger`. `matches_card_filter` reads eight
clauses off the permanent hosting the ability — `self_only`, `exclude_self`,
`attached_to`, `haunting`, `encoded_on`, the damage ledger, `controller`, and
`resolve_chosen_subtypes` — and a delayed ability has no such permanent. A
`condition` over the `subject` binding expresses the same filter exactly, which is
what Sea Gate Stormcaller uses and what the tests above pin; the cost is that every
card of this shape spells its filter as a condition rather than as a filter.

## `two_share_a_color` — "two cards that share a color"

### Overview

Sphinx's Tutelage: "If two nonland cards that share a color were milled this way,
repeat this process." The colour half of that sentence; the loop is
`repeat_while`.

### The shape

A condition taking a **pool**, true when any two members' colour sets intersect.
Pairwise and short-circuiting: the question is whether any two share, not how
many do.

It is the only colour question in the language that asks about a *relation
between two cards*. Every other reader is per-object, and each fails differently:

- `colors` / `not_colors` test a member against a colour fixed when the card is
  written. This card names no colour.
- `min_colors` counts the colours on a single card, so it answers "was a
  multicolored card milled".
- `shares_a_color_with` is the near-namesake and resolves its argument through
  `_bound_oid`, which reads one oid and returns `None` for a list. A `mill`'s `as`
  binding is always a list, so the clause matches nothing at all — a card that
  loads, prints the sentence and never fires.
- `distinct` is restricted to power and basic land type.

`exists` with a count is the tempting substitute and drops the colour clause
entirely: "two nonland cards were milled" is true on almost every mill.

Colourless cards share no colour with anything. That falls out of the intersection
being empty rather than being special-cased, and it is the printed ruling: two
artifacts do not continue the process.

### Guarded by

`tests/unit/test_two_share_a_color.py`: two greens sharing; green against red and
green against blue not sharing; both colourless cases; the `not_types` filter
applied before the pairing, including the one-card-left case; the counting
spelling kept as a live card and gaining on the exact board where the colour
clause does not; and the load-time guards, a bare `true` among them.

## `repeat_while` — "repeat this process"

### Overview

Sphinx's Tutelage: "Whenever you draw a card, target opponent mills two cards. If
